linear-elasticity.title: Hooke's Law for Uniaxial Deformation
linear-elasticity.meaning: In the linear elastic regime, mechanical stress is proportional to strain.
linear-elasticity.conditions: Small uniaxial deformation of a homogeneous material below its proportional limit; the material returns to its original shape after unloading.
linear-elasticity.units: σ and E: Pa; ε: dimensionless; L: m

bernoulli-equation.title: Bernoulli's Equation
bernoulli-equation.meaning: Expresses conservation of mechanical energy per unit volume in a flowing fluid.
bernoulli-equation.conditions: Steady flow of an incompressible, inviscid fluid along a streamline; the same constant applies throughout the flow only when the flow is irrotational.
bernoulli-equation.units: each term: Pa = J/m³; ρ: kg/m³; v: m/s; z: m

harmonic-oscillator.title: Harmonic Oscillator
harmonic-oscillator.plain: m ẍ + kx = 0; ω₀ = sqrt(k/m); x = A cos(ω₀t + φ)
harmonic-oscillator.meaning: A linear restoring force produces sinusoidal oscillations at the natural frequency.
harmonic-oscillator.conditions: There is no damping or external driving; the force is linear in displacement, and the parameters m and k are constant.
harmonic-oscillator.units: m: kg; k: N/m; x and A: m; ω₀: rad/s; φ: dimensionless

standing-wave-string.title: Natural Frequencies of a Stretched String
standing-wave-string.meaning: The boundary conditions select a discrete set of standing-wave frequencies on the string.
standing-wave-string.conditions: A uniform, flexible string with fixed ends, constant tension, and small transverse oscillations.
standing-wave-string.units: f: Hz; L: m; T: N; μ: kg/m

ideal-gas-law.title: Ideal-Gas Equation of State
ideal-gas-law.meaning: Relates the pressure, volume, particle count, and absolute temperature of a dilute gas.
ideal-gas-law.conditions: The gas is close to ideal: interactions between particles and their own volume can be neglected, and the system is in equilibrium.
ideal-gas-law.units: p: Pa; V: m³; n: mol; T: K; R: J/(mol·K); k_B: J/K; N: dimensionless

first-law-thermodynamics.title: First Law of Thermodynamics
first-law-thermodynamics.plain: ΔU = Q − W; W = ∫ p_ext dV
first-law-thermodynamics.meaning: The change in internal energy equals the heat supplied to the system minus the work done by the system.
first-law-thermodynamics.conditions: A closed system; the convention W > 0 is used for work done by the system on its surroundings; the integral describes volume work in terms of the external pressure.
first-law-thermodynamics.units: U, Q, and W: J; p: Pa; V: m³

entropy-balance.title: Entropy Change and the Second Law
entropy-balance.meaning: A change in the entropy of a state is calculated along a reversible path, while the total entropy of an isolated system and its surroundings cannot decrease.
entropy-balance.conditions: The initial and final states are equilibrium states; the integral uses a hypothetical reversible path, which need not be the actual process.
entropy-balance.units: S: J/K; Q: J; T: K

coulomb-law.title: Coulomb's Law
coulomb-law.meaning: Describes the electrostatic force on point charge 2 due to point charge 1 in a vacuum.
coulomb-law.conditions: The charges are at rest and their dimensions are small compared with their separation; r₂ − r₁ points from charge 1 to charge 2; the surrounding medium is a vacuum.
coulomb-law.units: F: N; q: C; r: m; ε₀: F/m

ohm-law.title: Ohm's Law and the Resistance of a Conductor
ohm-law.meaning: The voltage across an ohmic element is proportional to the current, while the resistance of a uniform conductor is determined by its geometry and material.
ohm-law.conditions: A linear ohmic regime with constant temperature and resistivity; the conductor is uniform and has a constant cross-sectional area.
ohm-law.units: V: V; I: A; R: Ω; ρ: Ω·m; ℓ: m; A: m²

capacitor-energy.title: Capacitance and Capacitor Energy
capacitor-energy.meaning: Capacitance relates charge to voltage, while the stored energy depends quadratically on either charge or voltage.
capacitor-energy.conditions: A linear capacitor of constant capacitance is charged quasistatically; losses and fringing effects are neglected.
capacitor-energy.units: C: F; Q: C; V: V; U_C: J

lorentz-force.title: Lorentz Force
lorentz-force.meaning: Electric and magnetic fields determine the change in momentum of a charged particle.
lorentz-force.conditions: A point particle of charge q in prescribed classical fields; at relativistic speeds, p is the relativistic momentum.
lorentz-force.units: F: N; q: C; E: V/m; v: m/s; B: T; p: kg·m/s

faraday-induction.title: Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction
faraday-induction.plain: ℰ = ∮ E · dl = −dΦ_B/dt; Φ_B = ∫ B · dS
faraday-induction.meaning: A changing magnetic flux produces a nonconservative electric field and an electromotive force.
faraday-induction.conditions: The loop C is stationary; the orientations of C and S are related by the right-hand rule; for a moving loop, the v × B contribution must be included.
faraday-induction.units: ℰ: V; E: V/m; Φ_B: Wb; B: T; S: m²

electromagnetic-wave-speed.title: Speed of an Electromagnetic Wave in Vacuum
electromagnetic-wave-speed.meaning: Maxwell's equations relate the speed of light to the electric and magnetic properties of vacuum.
electromagnetic-wave-speed.conditions: Linear electrodynamics in vacuum; in a material medium, the wave speed depends on the medium's dispersive properties.
electromagnetic-wave-speed.units: c: m/s; μ₀: N/A²; ε₀: F/m

snell-law.title: Snell's Law of Refraction
snell-law.plain: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂; n = c/v_phase
snell-law.meaning: Determines how the direction of a light ray changes at the boundary between two media.
snell-law.conditions: Homogeneous, isotropic media, a planar interface, and the geometric-optics approximation; both refractive indices are evaluated at the same frequency.
snell-law.units: n: dimensionless; θ: rad; c and v_phase: m/s

thin-lens-equation.title: Thin-Lens Equation
thin-lens-equation.meaning: Relates focal length to object and image positions and gives the transverse magnification.
thin-lens-equation.conditions: A thin lens, paraxial rays, and a consistent sign convention for real and virtual distances.
thin-lens-equation.units: f, d_o, and d_i: m; M: dimensionless

double-slit-maxima.title: Double-Slit Interference Maxima
double-slit-maxima.meaning: A path difference equal to an integer number of wavelengths determines the directions of the interference maxima.
double-slit-maxima.conditions: Coherent monochromatic light, identical slits, and the far-field regime; the diffraction envelope of each slit is treated separately.
double-slit-maxima.units: d and λ: m; θ: rad; m: dimensionless
